judge.reasoning: The answer correctly explains and represents the formula for MultiHead attention, explicitly using the Concat function as required.

rows.answer:
Multi-head attention is computed by concatenating the outputs of $h$ parallel attention heads and projecting the result:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h)W^O$$
$$\text{where } \text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$$

Where the projections are parameter matrices:
- $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$
- $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$

The system answer perfectly explains and mathematically defines the late-interaction operator using the maximum dot product.

rows.answer:
The late-interaction operator, $LI(q, d)$, is computed as the sum over all query token embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_q^{(i)}$ of their maximum dot product with each of the $N_d$ document token embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_d^{(j)}$. The formula is given by:

$$LI(q, d) = \sum_{i \in [1, N_q]} \max_{j \in [1, N_d]} \langle \mathbf{E}_q^{(i)} | \mathbf{E}_d^{(j)} \rangle$$
